criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
evidence: Historic archival photographs [1371, 1372, 1373, 1374] support brick, pale stone/concrete pilasters and horizontal bands, repeated rectangular windows, and a formal central entry.

Model uses brick-colored walling, light trim/bands, repeated windows, and a central door, but facade bays/windows are squat and regularized; the historical tall framed windows, strongly expressed monumental entry with broad steps, and characteristic proportions are absent or simplified.
Source photographs are historical qualitative evidence, not measured elevations or confirmation of current facade.

findings: The source-linked GIS outline and identity are unusually well documented, but the GIS area/perimeter summary fields conflict with the actual geometry ring.
Location/plan receives full credit based on exact ring-match evidence; positional accuracy still inherits the approximate, non-survey transform.
The principal visual shortfall is facade fidelity, especially the much more monumental entry and tall window/pilaster proportions seen in the archival photos.
The number of modeled facade bands does not substantiate the GIS six-level attribute; roof and height are only partly supported.
limitations: Visual assessment was made from saved front/isometric/top renders and archived photos; no interactive Blender session or measured elevation source was used.
The asset's exact source-ring geometry match is taken from its saved reopen-validation record, while source identity/attributes and archival visuals were independently inspected here.
